Program Description

Transform a two-year diploma from a recognized college into a university degree at the University of New Brunswick’s Faculty of Business.

The Bachelor of Applied Management (BAM) program is tailored to the needs of professionals and college students from any field who are interested in advancing their education, making a career change or advancing within their current workplace.

The BAM program provides students with a broader understanding of how key operations integrate in the business environment including:

  • Finance
  • Accounting
  • Human resource management
  • Marketing
  • E-commerce
  • Communications
njy:
The Bachelor of Applied Management in Accounting (BAMAC) program at the University of New Brunswick complements the practical and technical accounting experience gained through a college education with university-level studies in accounting.

The BAMAC qualifies students for greater career opportunities or to pursue a professional accounting designation, such as the Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA).

As an added bonus, all courses required for admission to the CPA program are offered!
nk3:
Program Description

Biology is the study of life. At UNB Saint John, Arts students can major in Biology, studying botany, ecology, zoology, organic chemistry and microbiology. Students will be able to explore the world of environmental science, sustainable development and public policies towards land and water use.

In a student's first year they will take introductory studies in organic chemistry, ecology cells and organisms and biology lab work. In second year they will add botany, microbiology, zoology and statistics to their course work and at the end of the year they may apply to major in Biology. Upper-level studies in Biology may include conservation biology, environmental law and animal behaviour.

A student's biology degree will teach them to analyze how living things work and interact with other organisms. students will learn to think critically and solve problems through observation and evaluation.

Program Description

Prepare for a complex, changing world with a degree that gives students the skills and hands-on experience to build a successful career.

UNB's Bachelor of Arts graduates know how to make a difference in their world. Their unique programs bridge fields of study and push the boundaries of traditional arts degrees. Get practical, hands-on experience that links classroom learning to the world beyond through community engagement in Saint John.

UNB encourages students to think critically and creatively while developing the research, analytical and communication skills they need to succeed. Communication Studies is online, interactive, and connected. Society is in the midst of a fundamental shift in how people communicate with each other, access information, and view popular culture.

As a Communication Studies student on the Saint John campus, students will cast a critical eye on the impact of new technologies and processes on the social, political, economic, and cultural landscapes.

Topics include the decline of newspapers, radio, and television; the rise of Twitter, Facebook, and other social media; the impact of mobile computing; and the eternal question of ‘do people control devices or do devices determine who people are?’

Unlike many similar programs, which focus on one discipline’s perspective, this program is multidisciplinary. This means students will learn about complex topics from multiple fields of study and perspectives, including Sociology, Psychology, and History.

Small classes led by accomplished academics and media practitioners will provide students with a unique amount of attention, encouragement, and mentorship.

  • Hands-on learning
  • Media internships
  • Work-study opportunities
  • Practicum courses
  • Other experiential learning opportunities
  • Skills acquired
  • Critical thinking and problem solving
  • Communication (written and oral)
  • Organizational
  • Interpersonal
  • Research and analysis
  • Media production techniques
nk6:
Program Description

Economics is about answering how and why. How and why do we produce, distribute, and purchase the goods and services? How and why do people address problems? How and why do people make decisions? When people attempt to answer those questions, they attempt to understand Economics.

In the Economics program at the University of New Brunswick Saint John, students will learn to use analytical, mathematical, and statistical techniques to answer questions and solve problems. Students will examine the roles individuals, consumers, small businesses, managers, CEOs, and politicians play in shaping both the Canadian and global economies.

Interactive classes with award-winning instructors provide opportunities for students to debate, question, and work closely with their instructors and peers.

Hands-on learning

  • Coursework involving case studies and group projects
  • Co-operative education (co-op) program

Skills students will acquire

  • Critical thinking
  • Problem solving
  • Judgement
  • Decision making
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Analytical
  • Mathematical and Statistical
nk7:
Program Description

UNB’s English program will expose students to literature that will deepen their understanding of different cultures and different people. It will refine their writing, oral communication, and critical thinking skills, show students how language is vital to daily life, and deepen their appreciation of beauty. Students will study poetry, drama, films, and fiction that anchor the collective imagination.

The faculty members have been recognized locally, regionally, and nationally for their excellence in teaching.

University of New Brunswick has developed innovative classes that enable students to debate, express, explore, and refine their ideas about the culture around them.

Hands-on learning

  • Opportunities to teach Shakespearean plays at local schools, as part of the Shakespeare and Pedagogy course
  • Coursework involving hands-on experience with live theatre
  • Opportunities to publish poetry in the VOX, the student creative writing journal

Skills students will acquire:

  • Close critical reading of complex materials
  • Critical thinking
  • Written and oral communication
  • Research and assessment
  • Creative writing
  • Understanding complex cultures
  • Organizational
  • Interpersonal
  • Research
6tsn:
Data science for finance: this is the best way to describe our Master in Quantitative Investment Management (MQIM) program. This one-of-a-kind one-year graduate program will prepare students for a specialized career in quantitative investment management. We equip our graduates with the fundamentals of finance knowledge, analytic and programming skills, and professional development competencies demanded by the finance industry.

Quantitative Investment Management integrates tools from finance, economics, applied mathematics, statistics and computer programming to address problems in derivative securities valuation, dynamic investment strategies and risk management. These skills are sought by investment and commercial banks, trading companies, hedge funds, insurance companies, corporate risk managers and regulatory agencies.

Our program graduates are currently working for asset management firms such as Vestcor Inc., AIMCo, quant shops, investment and commercial banks. Quantitative investment skills are in high demand!
8imv:
Training and education in cybersecurity falls far short of current needs, and what will be required in the future. Worldwide, there are 3.5 million unfilled cybersecurity positions. Such skills shortage leaves the public, private sectors, and governments vulnerable. Moreover, the global cost of cyber-attacks is believed to grow to $10.5 trillion by 2025. With these figures in mind, we need to develop talent in cybersecurity – and fast! The Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC) at the University of New Brunswick is using 20+ years of cyber- security innovation and talent development to provide a one-year Master of Applied Cybersecurity (MACSec).

The Faculty of Computer Science and CIC are partnering to develop talent – ready to contribute as cybersecurity experts.
8ij6:
Governments, non-profit organizations, and businesses invest significant time, money, and materials to implement policies and introduce programs that achieve their long-term strategic goals and address the needs of individuals.

For individuals interested in developing foundational research skills to address real-world questions across various applied settings, this program is suitable. In the MAPRE course and practicum-focused program, participants will have the opportunity to supplement their coursework with an extended practicum in a community setting.

A program accessible to all students

Students are not required to have an undergraduate degree in psychology. The MAPRE course and practicum-based program accommodates individuals from diverse academic backgrounds, equipping them with the skills necessary to conduct applied research in a variety of settings. In the program, recent university graduates and current professionals will collaborate and learn how to approach program evaluation and research through a team-based approach. Students can also select elective courses aligned with their personal interests and needs.

An emphasis on experiential learning

The program’s core focus is on experiential, hands-on learning. Throughout this one-year program, participants will have opportunities to integrate theoretical knowledge with practical experiences. Additionally, they will learn how to design program evaluations and gain knowledge about statistics and psychological testing to support their evaluations.

In the fall, students will choose where to complete their summer practicum. In the winter, they will work with the program coordinator and their community partner to develop a program evaluation proposal. After completing their coursework, students will then have the opportunity to work at their partner organization to conduct their program evaluation.

Unique to the Maritimes

The MAPRE program is the first of its kind focused on evaluation in the Maritimes. No other universities in the region offer graduate degrees in program evaluation, meaning residents of New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, and Nova Scotia often have to travel to other provinces for education in this field. The development of this program was driven by a clear regional need.

Community partners have reported to the MAPRE committee that they frequently send their employees out of province for evaluation training. This degree allows students to stay in the Maritimes while pursuing their graduate studies.
8iiy:
The Master of Computer Science program offers students the opportunity to explore advanced knowledge in computer science.

The Master of Computer Science by Coursework (MCSC) program provides advanced graduate-level education for students who wish to further their computer science education without engaging in research. It allows students to explore computer science topics in greater depth and learn current advanced techniques. This program is well-suited for individuals from the IT industry seeking to upgrade their skills, develop and demonstrate their capabilities for working at a more advanced level, explore specialized interests, and enhance their credentials.

The program requires a minimum of 10 graduate and undergraduate courses, in accordance with the master’s course requirements. Additionally, this degree can include a co-op designation, which is awarded upon the successful completion of two graduate co-op work terms.
8ij1:
This degree is tailored for future master’s-level practitioners, such as school counselors or counseling therapists working in community agencies or private practice. The MEd in Counselling also provides the option of a combined research and practice-based degree, which can serve as a foundation for pursuing doctoral studies in counseling psychology.

It is important to note that the MEd in Counselling is not designed to qualify individuals for licensure as psychologists.

Counselors work with individuals, groups, and families to address a wide range of issues related to daily life and development, including:

  • Career choice and adjustment
  • Successfully making life transitions
  • Functioning in interpersonal relationships
  • Emotional and behavioral problems

Faculty members conduct research on topics such as:

  • Career and vocational development
  • Counseling processes
  • Therapeutic relationships
  • Growth psychology
  • The practice of counseling and counseling psychology in Canada

The program offers two routes for students:

  • MEd course route: 10 courses (33 credit hours), including a six-credit-hour practicum
  • MEd thesis route: 10 courses plus a thesis (48 credit hours)
8ij4:
The Master of Education in Educational Administration and Leadership program is designed for professionals and academics seeking to advance their administrative and leadership capabilities within leadership roles.

The program enhances theory, knowledge, capacities, practices, and related skills through the exploration of school change and improvement, organizational behavior and theory, school governance, leadership roles, and cultural diversity.

Additionally, the program emphasizes leadership within the context of social justice and aligns with the latest regional, national, and international leadership standards of practice.

This area of study is of particular interest to professionals both in Canada and internationally, as there is a growing global demand for school leaders to obtain quality credentials.

Master of Education courses will be delivered online.
8iir:
The MEng degree is designed for students who wish to study one or more fields of geomatics engineering at an advanced level, gaining exposure to new geospatial technologies and a variety of application domains such as Remote Sensing and Computer Vision, Spatial Data Sciences, Geodesy and Positioning, and Hydrospatial Engineering. The course-based MEng program consists of 30 credit hours of coursework, selected in consultation with the Director of Graduate Studies.

The degree is intended to be completed in three or four academic terms, depending on the student’s background. Co-op work terms are also encouraged.

The Engineering Co-op Program allows students to develop as professionals and build critical transferrable skills, providing a competitive edge in the job market. Participation in the co-op program enables students to apply the theory and knowledge gained in coursework to a professional work environment. Students are advised to consult with their department and the co-op office to determine the length of co-op they qualify for under current regulations; however, all relevant work experience is considered beneficial and can support employment prospects after graduation.
86ak:
Advance your career with the MELDI program. It offers a comprehensive approach to engineering leadership with a combination of technical knowledge and business-savvy. Pursue advanced technical knowledge in one of four concentrations. Take courses in change management, leadership development, and design innovation.

Be prepared for the future of engineering with multi-disciplinary and interdisciplinary learning focused forward on turning global challenges into opportunities. Choose this intensive, high performance, premium program to give yourself the edge in engineering for the future.

Building Better Communities Concentration

If you're passionate about solving the housing crisis and creating future-proof communities, then this is for you. Explore new ways to accelerate construction while making it safer, greener and more sustainable. Design better homes and buildings, then expand your skills to build more resilient and fair communities for everyone.

Advanced technical course topics:

  • Advanced digital technologies in the built environment
  • Building sustainable and equitable communities
  • Construction materials for the future
  • Energy efficiency in building design
5s9z:
The program can be tailored directly to the student’s field of work, whether that is accounting, quantitative analysis, finance, or entrepreneurship.

The MBA program lasts 20 months — or four semesters — and comprises 18 courses. The first year establishes a solid foundation in business through 10 required courses. In the second year, students choose six elective courses and focus on their areas of interest through coursework, projects, or a combination of coursework and thesis.

Students will also develop a capstone project in their final year, working with real companies to develop and pitch a competitive strategic plan.

Program options

  • Concentration in Management Analytics: As digitization increases, organizations are changing rapidly, creating a significant demand for graduates who are tech-savvy and adept at interpreting large data sets.
  • Concentration in Venture Commercialization, Scaling, and Investment: This program is ideal for those eager to discover their entrepreneurial potential. It offers courses that provide the knowledge and skills necessary for a successful career, whether running a business or taking on leadership roles within existing companies.
  • MBA in Sport and Recreation Management: This specialization prepares students for careers in recreation and sport industries.
9hns:
The University of New Brunswick Saint John’s Accelerated Master of Business Administration (MBA) program pairs a world-class education with a personal, welcoming experience.

  • Immersive MBA (iMBA): In addition to completing the aMBA’s five modules, students selecting the iMBA, complete an additional four-month immersive experience designed to strengthen applied learning and market readiness. Students choose from one of three options, including a paid-internship, a faculty-supervised research project, or the development of a new entrepreneurial business venture.

This pathway provide a rigorous, applied and AACSB-accredited graduate business education.

Through advanced coursework, case analysis, simulations, applied business consulting practicums, and professional development, students gain the knowledge and competencies required to address complex organizational challenges and exercise effective leadership.

Students benefit from small class sizes, a diverse international cohort, accessible faculty, dedicated program staff and strong connections with the business community.

The curriculum emphasizes evidence-based decision-making, critical thinking, persuasive communication, ethical leadership and the integration of knowledge across business disciplines.
8ij5:
The Master of Business Administration (MBA) program develops innovative, entrepreneurial leaders through small class sizes, a diverse international student body, and access to faculty members who are leaders in their fields — all delivered in a one-year, accelerated format over 12 consecutive months.

Regardless of their chosen area of specialization, students gain access to networking opportunities, business consulting projects, and the chance to enhance their education through international experiences, all within an AACSB-accredited program. Students select one of seven specializations and complete 62.5 credit hours of academic coursework across five continuous semesters over a 12-month period, comparable to a two-year, four-term delivery model.
